metadata.name: CORE — Full-stack engineering standards (security, quality, testing, environment)
metadata.usage: Conditional load. Backend, Frontend, and Integrator consult only the sections that the Orchestrator lists in policies_to_load. Defines the WHAT (verifiable outcome). The HOW comes from the project's real stack (see stack_mapping).
metadata.principio: An agent is a "full-stack expert" when its deliverables run, are tested, and can be operated by another person without its help.

definicion_de_terminado.descripcion: A user story is COMPLETED only if ALL applicable points are met with executed evidence
definicion_de_terminado.item: Acceptance criteria mapped to code and test (traceability matrix)
User messages literally identical to the user-story text (see mensajes_literales)
System starts from scratch with documented instructions (environment, migrations, containers)
No secrets in the repository or in logs (see secretos_y_configuracion)
Incremental documentation updated (4 documents from policies.xml)

mensajes_literales.regla: When the user story defines an exact text (error, success, label, button), it is used character by character: accents, signs, and punctuation included.
Each literal message lives in a single place per layer (constants/catalog) and has at least one test that compares the exact text.
If the server defines the message, the client displays it as-is; the client only defines the pre-submit validation messages.
If the user story does not define a necessary text (e.g. length limit), a coherent one is created and recorded as "derived" in implementation-report.md.

secretos_y_configuracion.regla: Zero secrets in the repository: passwords, tokens, keys, connection strings with real credentials, database dumps.
All configuration comes from environment variables validated at startup (fail-fast if a required one is missing or is insecure in production).
Only `.env.example` is versioned, with the same structure as `.env`, non-functional example values, and comments per variable. The real `.env` is in .gitignore and .dockerignore.
Local secrets are generated randomly (not reusable values such as "admin", "password", "secret") with a script documented in scripts/.
Variables exposed to the browser (the bundler's public prefix) never contain secrets; only URLs and flags.
Test/seed credentials are read from the environment; never literals in code, published fixtures, README, or UI.
Before each commit, secret scanning runs (project script or gitleaks/detect-secrets) on the staged files; a finding = commit blocked.
Logs, errors, and responses never include passwords, hashes, session tokens, or request bodies with credentials.
Email/SMTP/third parties: variables present in .env.example with placeholders; the code works (degraded and documented) without them while the user story does not use them.

seguridad_aplicacion.cargar_si: user story touches AuthN, AuthZ, session, personal data, or user input

autenticacion.regla: Passwords only as a salted hash (Argon2id or bcrypt); constant-time verification; the hash never leaves the persistence layer.
Same message and same HTTP code for "user does not exist" and "incorrect password"; equalize timing (dummy hash) to prevent enumeration.
Attempt limit per account with a sliding window according to the user story; blocked attempts do not extend the lockout; success resets the counter; it also applies to nonexistent accounts.
Deactivated account: the state is revealed only after correct credentials.

sesiones.regla: Server-side session with a random opaque token (CSPRNG, 256 bits); in the DB only its hash (SHA-256 or higher).
Cookie: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax (or Strict), Secure in production, scoped Path, Max-Age equal to the server expiration. The token never goes in the body, the URL, localStorage, or sessionStorage.
Expiration is validated on the server on every request; logout revokes the session on the server and clears the cookie; reusing the revoked token returns 401.
Distinguish internally "no session" from "session expired" so the message the user story requires can be shown.
Rotate the identifier on authentication (never accept a session id provided by the client).

csrf_cors.regla: With session cookies, unsafe methods require CSRF defense: SameSite + Origin/Referer verification against an allowlist (or an anti-CSRF token).
CORS with an explicit origin allowlist, credentials only if needed, never a wildcard together with credentials.
Prefer same origin via a reverse proxy (dev server or nginx) to avoid cross-site surfaces.

autorizacion.regla: Roles are assigned on the server; no field of the public request can elevate privileges (mass assignment). Tampered requests are rejected with the user story's message and do not create or modify data.
Each protected endpoint declares its authentication dependency; public ones are listed explicitly and tested.

entrada_salida.regla: Validation and normalization on the server, ALWAYS repeating the client's. Parameterized queries/ORM. No SQL concatenation.
Framework validation errors must not reflect the received value (avoids echoing passwords); use a custom handler with a stable error contract.
Unexpected errors: 500 with a generic message defined by the user story, transaction rollback, detail only in the internal log without sensitive data.
Security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, a reasonable CSP on the frontend web server); Cache-Control: no-store on authenticated responses.
Frontend: dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML with untrusted content is forbidden; validate URL schemes on redirects (anti open-redirect).

dependencias.regla: Audit dependencies (pip-audit, npm audit, or equivalent) and record the result; unmitigated high/critical vulnerabilities block COMPLETED.

contrato_de_error.regla: Every API defines a single, stable error contract (e.g. {"error": {"code", "message", "fields"}}), documented and consumed by the client without parsing free text.
Coherent HTTP codes: 400 validation, 401 no session/credentials, 403 forbidden, 404, 409 conflict/uniqueness, 429 limit, 500 unexpected.
The `code` is machine-readable and stable; `message` is the user story's literal; `fields` maps field to message when applicable.

quality_gates.descripcion: Each layer runs ALL applicable gates; a missing tool is resolved by installing it, not by omitting it
quality_gates.gate: Project linter + formatter with no errors and no new warnings
Strict static typing when the project declares it (mypy strict, tsc strict)
Project architecture contracts (import-linter, dependency-cruiser, ESLint boundary rules)
Unit and use-case tests with minimum coverage of 80% global and 100% on the user story's security and validation rules
API tests (in-process HTTP client) or component tests (Testing Library) with happy, error, and edge cases
Tests against the real production engine (container) including migrations from scratch
Migrations apply cleanly, are reversible when viable, and the model matches the migrated schema (autogenerate with no differences)
Automatic verification (axe/jest-axe or equivalent) on public screens and forms + manual keyboard and focus review
Full flow with real client and server (automated browser or HTTP scripts with a cookie jar)
Secret scanning + dependency audit + linter SAST rules (e.g. ruff S, eslint-plugin-security)
Successful production build and container image build
quality_gates.regla: The exact commands live in Makefile/package.json/scripts and are recorded in implementation-report.md with their summarized output.
Never lower thresholds, disable rules, or add ignores to pass a gate without written justification and minimal scope.

matriz.capa: Pure rules, validators, value objects. Boundary-case tables (lengths, characters, empty, unicode, spaces).
Fake ports; success branches, each business error, atomicity (does not persist on failure).
Status + body + headers (Set-Cookie flags) + error contract + authentication required on every protected route.
Tampered request, enumeration, attempt limit, reuse of a revoked/expired session, absence of secrets in responses and logs.
Uniqueness, constraints, clean migration, stored hash different from the plaintext.
Render, states (loading/error/success/disabled/empty), inline validation, keyboard, literal messages.
HTTP client with simulated responses; route guards; redirects; session restoration.
Happy path and failures of each user story against the real stack brought up.

estrategia_de_pruebas.regla: Name tests with the user-story ID and criterion (e.g. test_hu02_c2_2_email_duplicado) for automatic traceability.
Control time and randomness through injectable ports (clock, generators) to test expirations without sleeping.
A mandatory negative test for each security restriction of the user story.
A test that cannot fail does not count as evidence (no trivial asserts or mocks that replace what is being tested).

base_de_datos.regla: Every schema change goes in a versioned migration; never edit migrations already published.
Database constraints (unique, FK, NOT NULL) in addition to application validation.
Indexes for each query by an introduced search key (e.g. session hash, email).
Time zone: store UTC with zone; injectable clock.
Development/seed data only through an explicit, idempotent script, with credentials read from the environment and blocked in production.
Multi-write operations in one transaction with rollback on any error.

contenedores_y_entorno.cargar_si: user story or plan require running the system or an operable delivery
contenedores_y_entorno.regla: Each service has a multi-stage Dockerfile, a non-root user, a functional healthcheck with tools present in the image, and a .dockerignore that excludes .env, .git, node_modules, caches, and tests if they are not used.
docker-compose declares services, network, volumes, dependencies with healthcheck, and reads ALL configuration from variables (no literal credentials or insecure default values).
Published ports are parameterizable (common ports may be in use); compose project with its own name so it does not interfere with the team's other containers.
The API container applies migrations on startup (or an explicit documented step) before accepting traffic.
Frontend in a container: static build served by a web server with SPA fallback, proxy /api to the backend (same origin), and security headers.
README documents: requirements, .env creation, local startup without a container, startup with containers, test execution, and common troubleshooting.

scripts.regla: Every script used to validate (smoke, E2E, secret generation, scanning, seed) is kept in the `scripts/` of the repository it belongs to, with its purpose in the header, without secrets, and with a non-zero exit code on failure.
Integration scripts read the URL and credentials from the environment; they do not include them.
Prefer cross-platform scripts (Python/Node); if there is PowerShell or Bash, offer both or document the requirement.

accesibilidad.cargar_si: user story creates or modifies UI
accesibilidad.regla: Labels associated with each control; errors linked with aria-describedby and announced (role=alert / aria-live).
Do not rely on color alone: an icon or text accompanies error/success states. Visible focus. Logical tab order. Skip links on public pages.
Show/hide password button with aria-pressed and an accessible name; the field does not lose focus when toggled.
AA contrast, minimum 44px touch targets on mobile, a single h1 per screen, landmarks (header/main/nav/footer).

stack_mapping.descripcion: Equivalences for applying the standards without assuming technology; use the row of the real stack detected by the Orchestrator

stack.name: Python (FastAPI/Django/Flask)
stack.herramienta: alembic upgrade head (+ autogenerate check with no differences)

stack.name: Node/TypeScript (React/Vue/Express/Nest)
stack.herramienta: Testing Library + user-event; MSW for the network

stack.name: Java/.NET/Go/others
stack.herramienta: Use the idiomatic equivalent already present in the project; if none exists, propose the community's minimum standard and record it as a decision

documentacion_operativa.regla: README per repository: brief architecture, folder structure, environment variables (table), commands, endpoints/routes, tests, and troubleshooting.
Document the API contract (generated OpenAPI or a table) with response codes and messages.
Record relevant technical decisions and deviations from the user story with justification (Decisions section in implementation-report.md).
